{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABYgvIbQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhCFLUI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 9, "title": "Redesign browser UI into polished Play and Debug experiences", "body": "## Problem

The current [saturn-rust browser demo](https://takahirox.github.io/saturn-rust/) is a working SH-2 homebrew emulator but its UI still reads as a developer test harness. The Star Collector canvas, Play button, long technical descriptions, boot/file selectors, instruction controls and always-visible register tables form one long column. The game is not the visual focus and a first-time visitor must sift through debugging details.

Improve the **layout, visual design and UX**, while preserving emulator behavior and the research/debugging interface.

## Expected outcome

A polished, responsive retro console player with **two distinct views**:

- **Play (the initial/default view):** Modern Console aesthetics inspired by [Afterplay](https://afterplay.io/) (restrained dark/charcoal palette, cool blue/cyan accents, generous space, typography, large centered game viewport); subtle Retro Arcade cues inspired by [webЯcade](https://play.webrcade.com/) without copying logos or third-party artwork. The prominent initial action is **Play Star Collector**.
- **Debug (on demand):** A purposeful, compact Emulator Studio layout for registers, CPU instruction stepping, boot-mode selection, local firmware/disc input, status/errors and frame advancement, taking functional cues from [EmulatorJS](https://emulatorjs.org/).

Do not build a game-library product, multi-theme system or CSS framework for the single-game demo. Prefer improving existing static HTML/CSS/JS.

## Context and reproduction

1. Open https://takahirox.github.io/saturn-rust/.
2. Note that a small 320×224 canvas and playable homebrew are buried among explanatory paragraphs, BIOS/disc controls, instruction stepping and CPU tables.
3. Narrow-screen layouts still expose all technical controls and create excessive vertical scrolling.

Inspect the current main branch before implementation:
- web/index.html: canvas with ID screen, Play Homebrew button, pause/frame controls, boot selectors, CPU registers and errors.
- web/style.css: a simple max-width 900px dark document without a distinct player shell.
- web/app.js: requestAnimationFrame, Wasm, keyboard-focus input, local ISO/BIOS reading, reset and asynchronous loading generation guards.
- scripts/browser-smoke.mjs: actual game and HLE/BIOS Playwright tests; public web/ asset allowlist and Pages subpath.
- docs/setup.md, AGENTS.md, docs/development-flow.md, docs/review-guidelines.md and the Issue template. Follow the repository's **English collaboration convention** and smallest-complete-change guidance.

This Issue concerns the frontend only, not new Saturn hardware, game compatibility or performance optimizations.

## Implementation requirements

### A. Play-first experience

- A compact branded header with Play / Debug navigation and low-key repository/source link. Brand as **saturn-rust**, not Sega; use original CSS/iconography only.
- On load, show Star Collector's title, short Saturn homebrew/HLE/silent-prototype disclosure, a large centered **native 320×224 canvas**, and an obvious **Play Star Collector** CTA. Canvas should resize responsively without stretching its 10:7 ratio or blurring its nearest-neighbor/pixel-art pixels.
- Once running, place functional **Pause/Resume**, **Reset/Restart** and **Fullscreen** controls adjacent to the player. Show a compact control hint: click/focus canvas, arrows move, Enter/Start restarts. Do not show fake sound control for a silent game or imply commercial game compatibility.
- Loading, paused/running, error and unsupported-hardware states must be visible and understandable near the player. Retain actual error text and provide ways to recover.
- Keep license, original guest source and downloadable sample ISO discoverable in a subordinate, compact information section. Preserve user-file privacy disclosures.

### B. Settings and local files

- A clearly discoverable **Load ISO / BIOS & boot settings** action opens an accessible disclosure/panel or correctly implemented modal (choose smallest maintainable approach). Reuse existing loaders, not a second code path.
- Preserve all three modes: BIOS-less HLE disc (supported 2048-byte-sector cooked ISO up to 16 MiB), HLE bootstrap debugger, and user-provided raw 512 KiB BIOS. Explain limitations and distinguish working HLE homebrew from incomplete native BIOS boot.
- Preserve locally read file bytes, validation errors, race cancellation, cold-reset semantics, and non-upload guarantee. No analytics, CDN, remote fonts, server uploads, browser storage or bundled Sega BIOS.
- Settings controls must work with keyboard and pointer, clearly indicate active mode and selected local file where appropriate, and not unexpectedly restart play on simply opening or dismissing settings.

### C. Dedicated Debug view

- Move CPU R0–R15 and special register tables, retired instructions, pending delay target, bounded Step/Run count, Reset, machine status, unsupported-opcode errors and frame advance controls out of ordinary Play mode.
- The HLE bootstrap fixture remains available and its **Run 6 → R0=4, R1=7, PC=0x0600000E** is visible. User BIOS mode must still load synthetic reset vectors and report unsupported opcodes accurately.
- Use a compact desktop panel/grid layout and readable single-column layout on small screens. Avoid updating invisible register tables each animation frame unnecessarily.
- **Play/Debug switching is presentational:** it must not reset the CPU, discard ISO/BIOS bytes, change boot mode or erase diagnostics. Specify predictable pause/focus behavior when leaving an active game (prefer pause/release held buttons).

### D. Interaction, accessibility and responsiveness

- Fullscreen targets the canvas/player shell using the browser Fullscreen API; provide truthful fallback when unavailable or denied, and restore layout/focus when exiting.
- Preserve keyboard input only when the game display is focused. When navigating menus, typing in a field, pausing, leaving the view or losing focus, release held game buttons so movement cannot become stuck.
- Use semantic headings/landmarks, explicit form labels, visible focus indicators, keyboard-operable controls, readable contrast, and live regions for errors/status. A modal, if used, requires accessible focus and Escape/close handling; no spurious machine reset when dismissed.
- At **1440×900**, **768×1024** and **390×844**, ensure no horizontal scroll, clipped canvas, overlapping or unreachable controls. Mobile layout must adapt, but virtual touchscreen game controls are not part of this Issue.
- Preserve static GitHub Pages deployment at /saturn-rust/, existing Wasm and CSP, and no additional UI framework or unnecessary dependencies.

### E. Tests and documentation

- Adapt scripts/browser-smoke.mjs to navigate Play, Debug and file settings while preserving tests that assert **real guest SH-2 gameplay** (move/collect five stars, score/completion, Enter to restart), HLE fixture state, BIOS and disc validation, local privacy, Pages subpath and MIME/asset checks.
- Add deterministic Playwright interaction checks for view switching without reset, pause and key release, settings/keyboard focus, fullscreen where supported, and Play-first initial state.
- Add automated responsive layout assertions for the three viewport sizes (canvas aspect ratio, useful visible controls, no document horizontal overflow); document limitations of any browser/Fullscreen test.
- Update README/setup to describe the Play/Debug navigation, load-image settings and how to reach the existing debug functions. Keep only needed runtime assets and update allowlist if files change.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] The default view is visually coherent and game-first; Star Collector title, Play CTA and a large pixel-crisp canvas are the primary visual elements, while CPU tables are **not visible** until Debug is selected.
- [ ] Play/Debug navigation and settings are discoverable and keyboard accessible, with clear focus and status. Switching views does not reset or change emulation mode, discard locally selected media, or leave directional input stuck.
- [ ] Working Play controls include start, pause/resume, restart/reset and fullscreen (or clear unsupported/denied messaging). Gameplay remains genuine guest execution with preserved input/score/completion/restart behavior.
- [ ] Debug exposes all existing CPU state and step/run/frame functionality; the six-step HLE reference state and user-BIOS reset/error paths remain testable.
- [ ] Local ISO and BIOS selection/validation, client-only file handling, async race protection, compatibility disclosures, and original asset/license links are maintained.
- [ ] Automated checks at desktop 1440×900, tablet 768×1024 and mobile 390×844 confirm responsive unclipped canvas, 320:224 ratio, usable controls, no horizontal overflow and working keyboard interaction.
- [ ] Existing native Rust, Wasm, and Playwright gameplay/BIOS tests pass with updated selectors/navigation and the GitHub Pages /saturn-rust/ path. The PR records real check results and any exclusions.
- [ ] The change is limited to the browser presentation and necessary tests/docs: no emulation core rewrite, game-library framework, unrelated optimization, fictitious sound/compatibility features, or proprietary visual assets.

## Optional validation

Before/after screenshots at desktop and mobile sizes and an additional browser are helpful but not a required human visual-approval gate. More advanced gamepad, touchscreen controls and theming can be separate tasks.

## Required post-merge verification

After the merge-triggered Pages deployment, verify on **https://takahirox.github.io/saturn-rust/** that the new Play-first UI loads, Star Collector remains playable, Debug/settings function and assets resolve at the project subpath. Record deployed revision and any production-only defects. Do not require production publication to pass before merge.
